claims.claim: Arethas was Archbishop of Caesarea Mazaca in Cappadocia (modern Kayseri, Turkey).
Arethas lived from approximately 860 to approximately 940.
Arethas was born at Patrae, Greece.
Arethas was a disciple of Photius.
Arethas became Archbishop of Caesarea early in the tenth century.
Arethas is considered one of the most scholarly theologians of the Greek Orthodox Church.
The Epigrammata consists of three epigrams numbered 15.32, 15.33, and 15.34 in the Anthologia Graeca.
The Epigrammata has a word count of 229.
Arethas was prominent in the revival of classical and patristic letters at Constantinople during the latter part of the 9th century.
Arethas was ordained deacon circa 895 and became court orator to the Byzantine Emperor Leo VI in 900.
Arethas was appointed to the See of Caesarea circa 903.
